introduction: “Grant us ears that are pure, hearts that are enlightened.” This guide gathers prayers for spiritual recognition: for eyes to see and ears to hear, for the veils of “vain imaginings” to be torn away, for the withered heart to be watered, for the grace to recognize God’s Manifestation and then to stand firm, and at the end for a lamp “in every world of Thy worlds”. People have prayed so for as long as there is record. “Lead me from the unreal to the real” is in the Upanishads; “Open thou mine eyes” and “Send out thy light and thy truth” are the Psalmist’s; the Fátiḥih asks to be shown the straight path. The Gospels tell of sight given: the blind man’s “that I might receive my sight”, “whereas I was blind, now I see”, the eyes opened at Emmaus; and Elisha prays that his servant may see what was always there. Plato’s cave and Blake’s cleansed doors of perception are the philosophers’ and the poet’s version. Jesus’s word to Peter, that flesh and blood did not reveal it, raises the question of what the seeker contributes; Newman asks only for the next step, and Tagore prays for the awakening of a nation’s mind.
questions: These prayers ask for sight, hearing and a pure heart rather than for information. What does that imply about why people fail to recognize the truth?
“Flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee.” If recognition is a gift, why pray for it, and what else do these prayers commit the one praying to do?
Elisha’s servant was shown what was already around him. What in ordinary life might be seen differently if prayers like reading 91 were answered?
Half of these prayers ask not for recognition but for steadfastness afterwards. Why is the second prayer needed once the first is granted?
Newman does “not ask to see the distant scene”. Reading 274 says “I know not what is within Thy Self.” How much does a person need to see in order to act?
Tagore prays that his country may awake into freedom of mind. How do the inward prayers of this guide bear on a society’s awakening?

outside.why: “Grant us ears that are pure, hearts that are enlightened.” Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.
The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.
The oldest prayer of this kind, from the Upanishads: lead me from the unreal to the real! Lead me from darkness to light! Lead me from death to immortality!
One who has believed and set himself toward Thee. Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
Aid the servant who has sought the light of Thy oneness. O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me.
Illumine their faces that they may behold Thee, and cleanse their hearts. Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
The plants in the hearts of Thy loved ones have withered; send down rain. Hopkins’s prayer in a dry season: birds build, but not I build; O thou lord of life, send my roots rain.
And Herbert, after such a season: who would have thought my shrivel’d heart could have recover’d greenness?
Let me not be among those whose ears are deaf and eyes blind. Moses to Israel: the Lord hath not given you an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.
Enable Thy servants to recognize the Manifestation of Thy Self. Paul’s prayer for his converts: the eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling.
Sanctify hearts from occupation with aught else. Teach me thy way, O Lord; unite my heart to fear thy name.
Lift from all eyes the veils of doubt. When it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.
“Leave me not to myself and my desires.” Our Lord! Cause not our hearts to stray after Thou hast guided us.
Knowledge led me to leave my home and set out toward Thee. Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, unto a land that I will shew thee.
Let the servant who has turned to Thee stand firm. He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.
Decree what will make me content with Thy decree. Not my will, but thine, be done.
Strength, that we may be steadfast. Unto him that is able to keep you from falling.
A testimony to be said daily. The prayer Muslims say in every act of worship: Thee alone we worship; Thee alone we ask for help. Show us the straight path.
By the Lamp of Thy Cause, which needs neither glass nor guard. The Qur’an’s lamp in its niche: light upon light. Allah guideth unto His light whom He will.
Cast me not out of the door of Thy grace. Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.
Send down what will purge them of all Thou abhorrest. A new heart also will I give you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh.
By the sighing of Thy lovers. My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee.
“Send down upon me that which will open mine eyes.” Elisha prayed for his frightened servant: Lord, open his eyes, that he may see. And he saw: the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire.
What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight.
“I am athirst; send down the rain of Thy grace.” I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground.
Assist me in the days of Thy Manifestation. Simeon, who waited a lifetime for it: mine eyes have seen thy salvation.
Increase his enkindlement with the fire kindled in Sinai. Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?
“Whose face is the object of my adoration, Whose beauty is my sanctuary.” One thing have I desired: to behold the beauty of the Lord.

Strip those who seek Thee of all that pertains to them. Donne asks for the same violence: batter my heart; o’erthrow me, and bend your force, to break, blow, burn, and make me new. Why do prayers for spiritual sight so often ask to be undone first?
Wandering in the desert of Thy love. I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
Mine eye expectant, mine ear longing. As the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, so our eyes wait upon the Lord.
At the break of every morn, set thy face toward the Kingdom. My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord.
“I have no refuge save Thee.” Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.
Hemmed in by difficulties, we have only to call. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord.
Set our feet firm and enlighten our hearts. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
Tear asunder the veil of vain imaginings that obscures the people’s vision. Plato’s prisoners take shadows for things, and one of them is turned round and led up into the light.
Blake: if the doors of perception were cleansed every thing would appear to man as it is, infinite.
Purge mine ear, that I may hearken. Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.
A new spirit, and eyes to behold Thy signs. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.
That which will assure their hearts and quiet their souls. Peace I leave with you; let not your heart be troubled.
The veil torn, that the longing may see. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him.
Turn our faces to the Beauty of Thy Oneness. God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts.

Enable Thy servants to recognize the Day-Star. When Peter recognized him, Jesus said: flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father. If recognition is given, what is the seeker’s part? What do these prayers ask the seeker to do?
“Thou hast removed the veil.” One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
Thanks for having been guided. He whose bosom Allah hath expanded, so that he followeth a light from his Lord.
“Praise be to Thee for having guided me.” I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
Blind are the eyes that see not the traces of Thy power. They seeing see not; and hearing they hear not.
But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.
Assist us to attain this bounty. Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find.
Enable us to conquer self and overcome desire. He that ruleth his spirit is better than he that taketh a city.
“I have tasted of the sweetness of Thy speech.” O taste and see that the Lord is good.

By the Name none has befittingly recognized. Paul found at Athens an altar to the unknown God: whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. Reading 229 calls even the recognized God unfathomed. What kind of knowing is being prayed for?
The stranger draws nigh, the sinner seeks forgiveness. God be merciful to me a sinner.
“No place is there for any one to flee to.” Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?
Suffer me not to be kept back. Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
Assist this servant to awaken those who sleep. Now it is high time to awake out of sleep: the night is far spent, the day is at hand.
“Write down for me what is best for me. I know not what is within Thy Self.” Newman, at sea and ill: lead, kindly Light; I do not ask to see the distant scene; one step enough for me.
Paul admits the same ignorance in every prayer: we know not what we should pray for as we ought; but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us.
“How can I remember Thee, knowing that my remembrance befitteth not Thy court?” Woe is me! for I am a man of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King.
A lamp in the light of Thy knowledge, to be with me in every world. Milton’s invocation: instruct me, for thou know’st; what in me is dark illumine.

Tagore’s prayer for awakening is for a whole country, and for its reason: where the mind is without fear and knowledge is free, into that heaven of freedom let my country awake. These prayers ask for inward light and for recognition of a Person. Does either kind of awakening lead to the other?

shortfall: The prayers of stretches two, eight and nine are largely petitions for steadfastness and service that ask by one Name after another, and many readings in the other stretches repeat the request for opened eyes; a companion was placed where a prayer brings its own image, and about a third were left without.

mark-that-i-might-receive-my-sight.text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? The blind man said unto him, Lord, that I might receive my sight. And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way

newman-lead-kindly-light.text: Lead, kindly Light, amid th' encircling gloom, / Lead Thou me on; / The night is dark, and I am far from home, / Lead Thou me on. / Keep Thou my feet; I do not ask to see / The distant scene; one step enough for me
newman-lead-kindly-light.author: John Henry Newman
newman-lead-kindly-light.work: The Pillar of the Cloud (“Lead, Kindly Light”)
